Covariance matrix (C backend)

Source: R/prim.R
ccovm.Rd

The covariance of every pair of columns of a numeric matrix or data frame. Column names are carried to both dimensions of the result.

Usage

ccovm(x)

Arguments

x

A numeric matrix, or a data frame of numeric columns (rows observations, columns variables).

Value

A symmetric ncol(x) by ncol(x) matrix.

Details

Entry \((j, k)\) is \(\frac{1}{n - 1} \sum_i (x_{ij} - \bar x_j)(x_{ik} - \bar x_k)\), as stats::cov() gives it; the diagonal holds the column variances. Missing values are not removed: an NA in a column makes every covariance with that column NA. A single row gives NaN throughout. A plain vector, and a data frame with a column that is not numeric, are refused.

See also

ccorr(), cmom().

Examples

X <- cbind(a = c(1, 2, 3, 4), b = c(2, 4, 7, 8), c = c(5, 3, 2, 1))
ccovm(X)
#>           a         b         c
#> a  1.666667  3.500000 -2.166667
#> b  3.500000  7.583333 -4.583333
#> c -2.166667 -4.583333  2.916667
all.equal(ccovm(X), stats::cov(X))
#> [1] TRUE
ccovm(data.frame(u = 1:5, v = c(2, 1, 4, 3, 6)))
#>     u   v
#> u 2.5 2.5
#> v 2.5 3.7
try(ccovm(1:5))
#> Error : ccovm: `x` must be a numeric matrix or data frame.
